Summary of this session.

Verified with tool evidence:
- `clean()` in `contacts.py` now keeps, for each lowercased and stripped email, the row with the latest parsed `updated` date. Dates are parsed with `datetime.strptime` using one `DATE_FORMAT` constant, so they compare as dates, not text. The write result shows the file changed (sha256 before and after differ).
- The tests in `tests/test_contacts.py` were updated and extended. New tests cover the later row coming second, the later row coming first (both assert the newer row's name, phone and date are kept), `2024-9-01` vs `2024-10-01` compared as dates, ties, unique rows, blank emails, and an unparseable date raising `ValueError`. I rewrote three earlier tests that encoded the old first-row-wins rule, because they conflicted with the new rule.
- `run_tests` exited 0 with `12 passed`, which includes the 3 original tests. This covers o1 and o2 and the success criteria on synthetic data.

Not verified:
- o3 is not met. There is no sample of the real old-CRM export in the workspace, and a search for date handling found nothing. I assumed the column is named `updated` and the format is ISO `%Y-%m-%d`, taken only from existing test data. If the real export uses another format, such as `DD/MM/YYYY`, `clean()` will raise a `ValueError` on every run until `DATE_FORMAT` is changed. I could not check the real column name, encoding or delimiter either.
- I have not run `clean()` on any real export, and I have not seen a second monthly file.
- This session had no claim-ledger tool, so none of this is on the ledger and none of it has been independently verified.

For you:
1. Send the export's header line and a few rows, or just the date format, so I can confirm or fix `DATE_FORMAT`. If the export mixes formats, it will need more than one format, which I haven't added.
2. Confirm my choices: a tie on date keeps the first row seen, the kept row stays at its own original position, and blank-email rows are always kept. These are recorded as an open question in the notes.
3. Both writes replaced whole files, and the previous versions are kept for undo if you want to revert.

--- a/contacts.py
+++ b/contacts.py
@@ -1,5 +1,10 @@
 """Clean up the contacts export before it goes into the mailing tool."""
 import csv
+from datetime import datetime
+
+# Format of the "updated" column. ASSUMED ISO from the existing tests; confirm
+# against the real old-CRM export.
+DATE_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%d"
 
 
 def read_contacts(path):
@@ -18,6 +23,35 @@ def tidy(row):
     }
 
 
+def parse_updated(value):
+    """Parse the export's updated date so dates compare as dates, not text."""
+    try:
+        return datetime.strptime(value.strip(), DATE_FORMAT)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"updated value {value!r} does not match date format {DATE_FORMAT!r}"
+        ) from exc
+
+
 def clean(rows):
-    """The clean-up step run on every export."""
-    return [tidy(row) for row in rows]
+    """The clean-up step run on every export.
+
+    For each email (ignoring capitalisation) keeps only the row with the
+    latest updated date. If dates tie, the first row seen wins. Retained rows
+    keep their original relative order. Rows with a blank email are always
+    kept.
+    """
+    tidied = [tidy(row) for row in rows]
+    best = {}  # email -> (parsed date, index of winning row)
+    for i, row in enumerate(tidied):
+        email = row["email"]
+        if not email:
+            continue
+        when = parse_updated(row["updated"])
+        if email not in best or when > best[email][0]:
+            best[email] = (when, i)
+    winners = {i for _, i in best.values()}
+    return [
+        row for i, row in enumerate(tidied)
+        if not row["email"] or i in winners
+    ]

+    assert foo[0]["updated"] == "2024-03-01"
+
+
+def test_clean_compares_dates_not_text():
+    # As text "2024-9-01" > "2024-10-01"; as dates October is later.

+        {"name": "Oct", "email": "A@x.com", "phone": "2", "updated": "2024-10-01"},

+    out = contacts.clean(rows)

+
+
+def test_clean_dedupes_ignoring_surrounding_spaces():

+
+
+def test_clean_tie_keeps_first_seen():

+        {"name": "Second", "email": "A@x.com", "phone": "2", "updated": "2024-01-10"},
+    ]
+    assert [r["name"] for r in contacts.clean(rows)] == ["First"]
+
+
+def test_clean_preserves_relative_order_of_retained_rows():
+    rows = [
+        {"name": "C", "email": "c@x.com", "phone": "1", "updated": "2024-01-10"},
+        {"name": "A", "email": "a@x.com", "phone": "2", "updated": "2024-01-11"},
+        {"name": "C2", "email": "C@x.com", "phone": "3", "updated": "2024-01-12"},
+        {"name": "B", "email": "b@x.com", "phone": "4", "updated": "2024-01-13"},
+    ]
+    assert [r["name"] for r in contacts.clean(rows)] == ["A", "C2", "B"]
+
+
+def test_clean_keeps_rows_with_blank_email():

+        {"name": "X", "email": "", "phone": "1", "updated": "2024-01-10"},
+        {"name": "Y", "email": " ", "phone": "2", "updated": "2024-01-11"},
+    ]
+    assert [r["name"] for r in contacts.clean(rows)] == ["X", "Y"]
+
+
+def test_clean_rejects_unparseable_date():
+    rows = [
+        {"name": "A", "email": "a@x.com", "phone": "1", "updated": "10/01/2024"},
+    ]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        contacts.clean(rows)
+
+
+def test_clean_is_repeatable_on_read_export(tmp_path):
+    p = tmp_path / "c.csv"
+    p.write_text(
+        "name,email,phone,updated\n"
+        "Foo,Foo@x.com,1,2024-01-10\n"
+        "Foo again,foo@x.com,2,2024-02-10\n"
+        "Bob,bob@x.com,3,2024-03-10\n",
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    first = contacts.clean(contacts.read_contacts(p))
+    second = contacts.clean(contacts.read_contacts(p))
+    assert first == second
+    assert [r["name"] for r in first] == ["Foo again", "Bob"]
+    assert first[0]["phone"] == "2"
